Q: Can't find Web Form item in Visual Studio A:

This is what worked in my case (Visual Studio 2026):

  1. Open VS2026 Installer and -having ASP.NET and Web development already installed- check, on the options at the right side- NET Framework 4.8 development tools (also there was for .NET Framework 4.7 and 4.6).
  2. Install this change.
  3. Run the installer again:
  4. Re-enable ASP.NET and web development (for some reason it got unchecked).
  5. Then, item templates appeared, so I selected and installed.
  6. When the installation finished, Add/Web Forms was available.

Q: Sorting by AM/PM time A:

My ActivityTime column is currently a string with HH:MM:SS AM/PM format

This is a deeply flawed schema design. Thanks to internationalization/localization and time zone issues, strings are almost always among the worst possible method for handling date/time and numeric data. This is a significant source of bugs, as well as worse for performance. Never NEVER NEVER store date/time or numeric values as strings.

BigQuery has both Time and DateTime types. Use them. It's far more efficient to parse input values to these types at create/update time than it is to reparse values over and over at read time, plus you'll have fewer bugs and do faster and more accurate date math.

Using strings can also subtly create MASSIVE performance impacts in the case where you may even need to parse every row in a table in order to accurately compare the stored values with an input or value from another table/column, even when the query only needs a few rows for the results. If things are already set with a date/time, no conversion is needed.

You really only ever want to deal with this stuff as strings at the last possible moment before showing it to a user or exporting it for another system.

Q: TLS handshake failed with error tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake server=Orderer remoteaddress=192.168.144.4:43496 A:

I met this issue before, and fixed it successfully. My solution:

  • first you need to check everywhere protocol you want to call the peer or the orderer with. The correct protocol is grpcs not grpc;
  • then you need to check the TLS Certificate you was using to call the peer or the orderer. Normally they are under the msp/tlscerts folder.

Q: Android SDK folder structure A:

It's not a guaranteed standard, but the folders have been consistent for many years now. Here are the core basics, see the links for more info: 

 # platform-tools: Updated each AOSP version; always backwards compatible
 # tools/bin: Platform-independent tools to help building/using android
 #            eg lint, sdkmanager, monkeyrunner
 # build-tools/<version>: Compilation tools, required to build.
 #            AOSP version specific, typically used by AS directly

See https://developer.android.com/studio/command-line/ https://www.programering.com/a/MDMyMzNwATk.html
